title: Time-Bound Reasoning Drills
tagline: Year 4 — Short reasoning items to be done in 30–45 seconds, and a method for pacing a reasoning section

introduction.overview: In a timed reasoning section, quick items (series, odd-one-out, ranks, directions, coding, simple relations) should take 30–45 seconds each, leaving the saved time for puzzles. This chapter is a drill of such items, together with a simple pacing method: classify each question on a first glance, do the quick ones first, and mark puzzles for a second pass.
introduction.placementRelevance: Online reasoning sections give about a minute per question on average; quick items bank time for the long puzzles.
introduction.realWorldContext: Triage under time pressure is a general workplace skill.

learningObjectives: Solve quick items in under 45 seconds
Classify a question at first glance
Use two passes through a section
Estimate time left per remaining question

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Time per remaining question = time left ÷ questions left.

coreDefinitions: Quick item: solvable in under 45 seconds.
Pass: one run through the section.
Triage: deciding which questions to do now.
Checkpoint: a planned time for progress review.
Time budget: total seconds divided by questions.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: The score comes from marks per minute. Quick items have the highest marks per minute.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: On the first glance classify: quick, medium, puzzle. Do quick ones, then medium, then puzzles with the time left.

mainNarrative: A section of 30 questions in 45 minutes gives 90 seconds each. Quick items should take 30–45 seconds, which saves 45–60 seconds on each.
Do a first pass: quick items and medium items. Mark puzzles with more than five clues for the second pass.
At the 30-minute mark, suppose 8 questions remain and 15 minutes are left: 900 ÷ 8 = 112 seconds each.
If a puzzle has gone past about 3 minutes with no progress, leave it and return.
Practise quick items daily until they take under 40 seconds.

deepDiveAspects.title: Marks per minute
deepDiveAspects.content: Quick items earn the same marks as hard ones in a fraction of the time.

deepDiveAspects.title: Second pass
deepDiveAspects.content: Puzzles returned to later often look simpler after a break.

placementStyle.question: Pointing to a man, a woman says, "He is the son of my mother's only child." The man is her
placementStyle.explanation: Her mother's only child is herself, so the man is her son.

placementStyle.question: How many triangles are there in a figure formed by joining the three vertices of a triangle to a point inside it? (count all)
placementStyle.explanation: Three small triangles plus the outer triangle: 4.

placementStyle.question: A clock shows 6:00. The angle between the hands is (degrees)
placementStyle.explanation: At 6:00 the hands are opposite, so the angle is 180°.
